neg11.clause_name: Risk Bullet – Free Time and Supervision
neg11.label: NEGATIVE

judgments.title: Free time disclaimer for during-course periods is weaker than before/after
judgments.reason: The provision identifies free time “before, during and after” the course but expressly disclaims responsibility only “before and after”; that enumeration raises an expressio unius question about responsibility during the course.

judgments.title: NOLS Disclaims Responsibility for Staff During "Free Time"
judgments.reason: The issue challenges the fairness and legal effect of characterizing staff as private individuals during free time, but the disclaimer itself is not ambiguous or inconsistent with another operative term.

judgments.title: Contractor liability disclaimer should be strengthened
judgments.reason: Whether the disclaimer defeats non-delegable duties is a legal-enforceability concern; the existing statement that NOLS is not responsible for contractor conduct is textually clear.

judgments.title: NOLS Disclaims All Responsibility for Contractors
judgments.reason: The issue seeks to impose a duty of reasonable contractor selection despite the disclaimer. That is a negotiation and enforceability concern, not a textual construction defect.

neg15.clause_name: Acknowledgment and Assumption of Inherent and Other Risks
neg15.label: NEGATIVE

judgments.title: Overly Broad Assumption of All Risks
judgments.reason: “ALL risks,” reinforced by “inherent or otherwise,” is deliberately broad rather than ambiguous. Whether that allocation is enforceable or overreaching is not a Category 1 or 2 defect.

judgments.title: Released Parties definition should include independent contractors and successors
judgments.reason: The omission of contractors, successors, and assigns from the defined Released Parties is a negotiation gap, not an ambiguity or conflict. The contractor disclaimer can operate independently of the release.

judgments.title: Indemnity should cover "reasonable" attorney's fees and costs
judgments.reason: The absence of a reasonableness qualifier affects the breadth or enforceability of the fee obligation, but the existing phrase “costs and attorney's fees” is textually intelligible.

judgments.title: Release should expressly survive course completion
judgments.reason: Express survival language may strengthen the release, but its omission does not create a textual contradiction or genuine ambiguity about claims arising from course participation.

judgments.title: Release carve-out for "lands whose rules or regulations prohibit" is vague
judgments.reason: The phrase “lands whose rules or regulations prohibit such agreements as a matter of law” is vague about which land-based rules, regulations, agencies, or legal regimes trigger the carve-out.

judgments.title: Internal drafting note - indemnity definition
judgments.reason: The parenthetical reads as an operative explanation of “indemnify,” not necessarily an internal drafting note. Whether it should be removed is an editorial issue; its malformed quotation is separately addressed in issue 36.

judgments.title: Broad Indemnification Obligation on Student
judgments.reason: The indemnity lists claims by family members, rescuers, and other students before adding “any other person,” creating a classic question about whether the catch-all is limited by the preceding classes.

judgments.title: Release of Negligence Claims is Overreaching
judgments.reason: The agreement expressly includes ordinary negligence and excludes gross negligence and intentional wrongdoing. The issue objects to that clear allocation rather than identifying ambiguity or conflict.

judgments.title: Inconsistent capitalization: Release and Indemnity
judgments.reason: The capitalization variation does not reasonably suggest two different sets of release and indemnity agreements in context, so it does not alter meaning.

judgments.title: Punctuation error with parenthetical definition
judgments.reason: The malformed opening “7indemnify” in place of an opening quotation mark is a mechanical punctuation or transcription error in the parenthetical definition.

neg17.clause_name: Other Provisions – Medical Fitness and Disclosure
neg17.label: NEGATIVE

judgments.title: Agreement places burden on student to determine age of legal competency
judgments.reason: This issue concerns allocation of the burden of verifying contractual capacity and the resulting enforceability risk, not ambiguity or internal inconsistency.

judgments.title: Inconsistent capitalization: student
judgments.reason: Lowercase uses of “student” plainly refer to the student described by the agreement; the capitalization inconsistency does not alter meaning.

judgments.title: NOLS Disclaims Any Role in Assessing Student Suitability
judgments.reason: NOLS's collection of health information and reserved removal right can coexist with the student's responsibility for determining suitability; those provisions do not directly contradict the disclaimer.

judgments.title: Removal provision should clarify no refund obligation
judgments.reason: The agreement's silence about refunds following removal is a missing commercial term, not an intrinsic ambiguity or contradiction with another provision.

judgments.title: Undefined term: Medical Protocols
judgments.reason: “Medical Protocols” refers to an unidentified body of written procedures, leaving uncertain which protocols govern and what medical conduct they authorize.

judgments.title: Unrestricted Right to Remove Student Without Refund Provision
judgments.reason: The broad removal discretion and absence of a refund promise are unfavorable terms or omissions, but they do not create a textual ambiguity or internal contradiction.

judgments.title: Broad Medical Authorization Without Limits
judgments.reason: The catch-all “other medical care” follows “emergency hospitalization” and “surgical” care, leaving its scope open to construction by reference to the listed forms of care.

judgments.title: Undefined term: Medical Protocols
judgments.reason: The unidentified capitalized term “Medical Protocols” leaves uncertain which written procedures govern NOLS staff's provision of medical care.

neg19.clause_name: Use of Contact Information and Images
neg19.label: NEGATIVE

judgments.title: Medical costs provision lacks specificity on evacuation expenses
judgments.reason: The provision clearly includes evacuation costs; failing expressly to add separately billed search-and-rescue costs is an omission in coverage, not a construction defect.

judgments.title: Image/likeness release lacks perpetual and irrevocable language
judgments.reason: The authorization that NOLS “may use” the information and images does not specify its duration or whether consent can be revoked, leaving the temporal scope of “may use” uncertain.

judgments.title: Contact info sharing provision is overly broad and may raise privacy concerns
judgments.reason: The phrase “strategic partners in which NOLS graduates may be interested” has uncertain boundaries and does not identify what relationships qualify as strategic partnerships.

judgments.title: Unlimited Medical and Evacuation Cost Obligation
judgments.reason: The phrase “costs reasonably associated with medical services” has an evaluative boundary that may require construction, including how closely evacuation expenses must relate to medical services.

judgments.title: Sharing Contact Info with Third Parties Without Consent
judgments.reason: The provision clearly permits sharing without a separate opt-in. The issue concerns privacy policy and consent allocation, not ambiguity or inconsistency.

neg20.clause_name: Responsibility for Damage to Facilities or Gear
neg20.label: NEGATIVE

judgments.title: Personal property disclaimer should extend to field operations
judgments.reason: The disclaimer unambiguously applies to belongings stored at NOLS facilities. Its failure to cover field operations is a scope limitation, not an ambiguity.

judgments.title: Unrestricted Use of Name, Image, and Contact Info
judgments.reason: The statement that NOLS “may use” the student's name and image provides no stated duration or revocation rule, leaving the continuing scope of the permission uncertain.

judgments.title: Student Responsible for All Damage to NOLS Gear Without Limitation
judgments.reason: The term “damage” may reasonably raise a boundary question over whether ordinary wear and tear or expected degradation from authorized use counts as damage caused by the student.

judgments.title: NOLS Not Liable for Student's Personal Belongings
judgments.reason: The disclaimer plainly states that NOLS is not responsible for loss, theft, or damage to stored belongings. Whether it can lawfully encompass NOLS's own negligence is an enforceability issue.

judgments.title: Exclusive Wyoming Venue May Be Inconvenient
judgments.reason: The Wyoming-only venue requirement is clear; inconvenience to an out-of-state student is a negotiation concern rather than a construction defect.

pos2.clause_name: Other Provisions — Governing Law and Forum Selection
pos2.label: POSITIVE

judgments.title: Continuation of personal property disclaimer
judgments.reason: Extending the disclaimer to field operations and transit would expand NOLS's protection, but the current facility-storage limitation is clear.

judgments.title: Spelling error in verb
judgments.reason: “Shal]” is a mechanical spelling or transcription error in the operative forum clause, corrupting the mandatory verb “shall,” even though the intended reading is apparent.

pos3.clause_name: Final Provision — Binding on Heirs, Estate, Executors and Administrators

judgments.title: Severability clause should include reformation language
judgments.reason: The severability clause clearly preserves the remainder of the agreement. Failure to authorize judicial reformation is an omitted remedy, not a construction defect.

judgments.title: Agreement Binds Heirs and Estate
judgments.reason: The extension to heirs, the estate, executors, and administrators is explicit. Its effect on independent statutory wrongful-death claims concerns enforceability and governing law, not textual ambiguity.
